items.title: Generative AI on This Crown's Cover
items.excerpt: Ilona Andrews says the cover of 'This Crown Will Not Rule Me' contained generative-AI elements despite no-AI clauses in both the authors' and Tor's contracts; Tor says the AI use happened without its or the authors' knowledge and is commissioning a replacement cover and tightening art review.
items.rationale: Primary-source statement on a concrete new incident: a Big Five imprint (Tor) is pulling an AI-tainted cover despite contractual no-AI clauses and tightening its art review, a practical lesson for cover sourcing.

items.title: COPYRIGHT NEWS—Anthropic and Meta self-helped themselves to AI training materials, new lawsuit asserts
items.excerpt: Carlson LLC, copyright owner of Richard Carlson's 'Don't Sweat the Small Stuff' series, sued Anthropic and Meta in N.D. Cal. (3:26-cv-14248, filed Nov 19), alleging more than two dozen self-help books were taken from Books3/Anna's Archive and scanned to train AI models; Carlson opted out of the Bartz settlement.
items.rationale: A new filing (Nov 19) by a different plaintiff that also names Meta. It shows opt-outs from the Bartz settlement turning into standalone suits, which matters to any rights holder weighing the settlement.

items.title: Australian Society of Authors, Australian Publishers Association among orgs launching 'Not AI's to Take' campaign
items.excerpt: The ASA, APA and media and creative bodies launched the 'Not AI's to Take' petition urging Canberra to keep copyright protections and require permission before AI firms train on Australian creative work; reports say music has since won a carve-out.
items.rationale: A new coordinated campaign launch by Australia's author and publisher bodies on the AI-training exception. It goes beyond the 10-24 Authors Guild statement and the 09-22 criticism story.

items.title: Namoo - 부모님의 이야기를 AI 인터뷰로 기록해 이북과 오디오북으로 만들어 주는 앱
items.excerpt: Namoo, a Korean indie app launch, runs AI interviews with parents about their lives and turns the transcripts into a memoir ebook and audiobook, a consumer take on AI ghostwriting.
items.rationale: A new product launch that adds a tool angle to a mostly policy-heavy day: AI-interview memoir creation that outputs both an ebook and an audiobook.

items.title: 'It's like the wild west': how AI has rocked the literary world
items.excerpt: Guardian interactive feature on AI across publishing: an indie author producing hundreds of AI books a year, literary agents with no reliable process for AI submissions, and the industry's scramble to set rules.
items.rationale: A reputable, in-depth industry feature. Its fresh element is how literary agents are handling AI submissions with no reliable process, which none of the published overviews covered.
